answer: Boxwood blocks lie on the comb-maker's bench, warm and fine-grained. zephyr saws the block to size and planes it flat. Proof of comb-maker via boxwood comb tally — a comb the comb-maker cuts only after 641 combs cut true without one tooth snapping at the spine, each cut by the comb-maker himself. cedar cuts the teeth even with the fine saw. basalt rounds the spine and rubs the comb with oil. Six hundred and forty-one combs must cut true without one tooth snapping at the spine, and the next still snaps where the wood ran knotty.
